Game tracking summaries

Source: R/game-tracking.R
nhl_tracking_summary.Rd

The NHL's tracking vendor writes three files per game alongside the play-by-play, at live.nhle.com/ppt/{season}/{game}. NHL.com's tracking module reads them; they are not among the NHL EDGE endpoints.

Usage

nhl_tracking_summary(game_id)

nhl_tracking_player_stats(game_id)

nhl_tracking_entities(game_id)

Arguments

game_id

Ten-digit NHL game id.

Value

nhl_tracking_summary(): a list of tibbles, players, teams, puck and info. The others: a tibble.

Details

  • nhl_tracking_summary(): each player's game from the tracking: time on the ice, top and average skating speed, distance, time and shift starts in each zone, and puck possession time (in all, by zone and by strength), with each club's possession time and share by zone and strength, and the puck's own top speed.

  • nhl_tracking_player_stats(): the vendor's box score: ice time by strength (5v5, 5v4, 4v5...), shifts and their lengths, faceoffs by zone and strength, shots by strength, and each shift as a list-column.

  • nhl_tracking_entities(): who the tracking follows: players (with their NHL id, height, weight, handedness), officials and the puck.

Speeds are in miles per hour (speed_max_mph, speed_avg_mph; the files keep feet per second), distances in miles and feet, times in seconds.

Coverage: the summaries and player stats exist for most regular-season games from 2021-22 to 2023-24, some of 2020-21 and 2024-25, and none from 2025-26 on, when only the entity list is still written. Playoff games are mostly missing.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
tr <- nhl_tracking_summary(2023020500)
tr$teams[, c("team", "possession_pct", "possession_pct_o_zone")]
top <- tr$players[order(-tr$players$possession_time), ]
top[, c("name", "team", "possession_time", "speed_max_mph", "distance_miles")]
}
